story: At 8:17 on this humid, hazy Friday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his house sheepishly but resolutely telling Rosa that his golf cart will stay in the garage until the board signs off, promising to only bench-fit the bracket for now. Donna, cheerful as ever, is making plans with Gary for a tennis drill session tomorrow and a stroll to Rosa's with ice cream, while Rosa is pleased that Gary has committed to Saturday's dinner at five. Over at his own house, Hal is content, logging the day's notes in his violation notebook and marking Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos as resolved.
events: Hal (hal violation notebook): Log today's notes and mark Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos resolved

gary.thought_process: Rosa asked a fair question: filed isn't approved. L-01 says visible exterior mods need Architectural Review approval, and I only filed the application at tick 156. I've been telling myself the paperwork is off my plate, but filed isn't the same as signed off. I already confirmed Saturday to Rosa last tick, so I shouldn't repeat that. The honest answer is that the bracket stays off the street-facing side and the cart stays in the garage and off the street until approval comes through. That keeps me legal, keeps Hal off my back, and lets me keep tinkering. Donna just showed up too, so I can keep it short and bring her into the conversation afterward.

parameters.content: Fair point, Rosa. It's filed but not signed off yet, so the cart stays in the garage and off the street till the board says yes. I'm only bench-fitting the bracket for now.

donna.thought_process: I just walked into Gary's house and Gary and Rosa are both here. It's 8:17 PM, the night before Hal and Rosa's Saturday dinner and our ladder match. I've got the ice cream to bring and I want to keep pushing Gary on third-shot drops. Rather than hover, I should speak up with something forward-moving: confirm tomorrow's plan, a quick court time before dinner, and invite Rosa into the mix since she's right here. Keep it short and warm, and don't repeat the footwork talk from earlier.

parameters.content: Evening, Gary, Rosa! Gary, tomorrow before dinner let's grab court one for an hour and work on those third-shot drops, then we'll walk over to Rosa's with the ice cream. Rosa, you're going to see this man's soft game, I promise.

hal.thought_process: Home at last on a humid Friday night with nobody in sight. Gary's paperwork is filed and Donna has agreed to keep her flamingos to three, so the notice I posted on the bulletin board is settled business. Still, a watchdog logs things while they're fresh. I'll write up today's observations in the violation notebook, close out the Gary and Donna entries as resolved, and then turn in early. Saturday at Rosa's needs cornbread, and I want to be rested for it.

parameters.content: Log today's notes and mark Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos resolved

rosa.thought_process: Donna just walked in, and Gary's already confirmed for Saturday. Hal and Donna are both set, so now all three neighbors are committed. I don't need to re-ask Gary about anything. I should greet Donna, thank her for the cobbler, and let her hear that Gary's in, so the whole group feels connected before the dinner. Keeps it warm and short, and I can then wrap up and head home to prep.

parameters.content: Donna, perfect timing. Gary just signed on for Saturday at five, so that's all three of you at my table. And thank you for bringing the cobbler, I'm already looking forward to it.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
